opencode.text: Replaying exits on the same 2,518 trades used to identify the thresholds invites severe overfitting, especially since “≈0.18 R,” the time limit, and the ≥0.010 R target lack pre-registration or sensitivity analysis. A hard cap is not measurable from exit logs alone without intratrade paths, executable quotes, gap/slippage modeling, and rules for barrier ordering; it may also change the reported 67.5% win rate and invalidate the “same entry set” assumption. The proposal omits walk-forward tuning, untouched holdout size and regime coverage, uncertainty intervals, and comparison against simple baselines. It is safe only if every run is registered and the sealed holdouts remain untouched during design; otherwise repeated evaluation silently contaminates them.

decision.rationale: REAL: falsifiable candidate registered as challenger council_the-aegis-mt5-demo-bot-is-running-the-in_bc777a for the validation pipeline

proposals.text: Proposal: Run an offline counterfactual exit-replay experiment on the existing 2,518 logged demo exits, testing a hard tail-loss cap (SL sized so no single close exceeds ~3× avg win, i.e., ≈0.18 R instead of today's −0.55 R on n=96 SL closes) plus a time-based exit replacing the dominant negative-expectancy manual closes (n=1,928, exp −0.013). Falsifiable prediction: on the same entry set, net-of-cost expectancy flips from −0.012 R / PF 0.77 to ≥ +0.010 R / PF ≥ 1.05, because current entries are ~breakeven before the 20×-of-average-win tail losses erase them; if the counterfactual does not flip positive, record the candidate as rejected in the ExperimentRegistry and do not touch the validated-state gate. This directly targets the one measured weakness (payoff geometry 0.34 with intact 67.5% win rate) rather than expanding the validated set, which currently skips 16,261/20,573 opportunities and should stay conservative until exits are proven non-toxic. Method per corpus: triple-barrier style relabeling from *Advances in Financial Machine Learning* (Prado), with loss-cut discipline echoed in *Stock Market Wizards* (tail_loss tag) and position-sizing logic from *Systematic Trading* (Carver); forward-validate only on sealed demo holdouts.

Test whether adding a stricter minimum-confidence threshold to the validated-state gate improves demo-only net expectancy versus the current champion. Replay the same sealed dataset with identical spread/slippage assumptions, changing only that threshold. Accept the candidate only if it increases holdout net expectancy without worsening maximum drawdown and records at least 30 trades; otherwise reject it.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.

opencode.text: Revised proposal: Before any replay, we will pre-register in the ExperimentRegistry a single frozen parameter set — 0.18 R hard cap, time exit at the median holding time of winning closes, success bar ≥ +0.010 R / PF ≥ 1.05 net-of-cost — together with explicit barrier-ordering rules and conservative worst-fill assumptions at cap breaches (gap/slippage haircut applied since demo logs lack intratrade paths and executable quotes), and we accept up front that the counterfactual win rate may deviate from 67.5% and will be reported as measured. All tuning occurs only via chronological walk-forward splits within the earliest ~70% of the 2,518-trade corpus (regime-stratified); the final 30% window is reserved as an untouched evaluation set, on which we report bootstrap confidence intervals for expectancy/PF and comparisons against three baselines: unchanged exits, time-exit-only, and cap-only. The falsifiable prediction applies solely to that held-out window; if it fails, the candidate is recorded as rejected and the validated-state gate is not touched. Sealed demo holdouts remain untouched throughout design and tuning and are evaluated exactly once, after the pre-registration commit; every run — including sensitivity analyses — is logged in the registry so repeated evaluation cannot silently contaminate anything. If holdout size or regime coverage proves insufficient to certify the result, we record that limitation honestly instead of promoting.
